approval_required_for: Any architecture, pipeline topology, memory-layout, runtime-ABI, numeric-policy, or major-template change proposed instead of a localized implementation repair. Approval must create a replanned or new contract where required, not mutate the active repair identity.

Any proposal to change the checkpoint, stimulus, independent target-model reference, frozen tolerance, semantic-testbench contract, or exact sample-project wrapper/source identity. Such changes are forbidden inside the current repair loop and cannot be used to make DUT output pass; an approved change must start a new contract.
Any ambiguous board/app-shell target or exact-wrapper selection after bounded discovery using user materials and real tool evidence; the target must not be guessed.
Any expansion from the localized causal module and its transitive dependents to broad RTL churn or unconditional reopening of passed layers.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not promote this refinement or enable certificate reuse. Preserve the prior artifacts, report the exact failed policy checker, and rerun only that checker after correcting the policy artifact; do not create a hardware repair request.
executable_actions.rationale: Materialize one checker-grounded policy with the ordering identity validation -> operator-leaf validation -> single-layer validation -> board AXI/DDR validation. The route matrix must distinguish evidence/checker defects from real hardware failures, require an earliest causal boundary, and prohibit lower-layer repair without contradiction and replay evidence.

consumes: current DUT loader and weight-binding manifests
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep every affected certificate at current_contract_valid=false and reuse_allowed=false. Classify absent target-model execution, catalog coverage, semantic harness, or consumption instrumentation as a checker/golden-reference capability repair rather than hardware failure. Never substitute random or RTL-derived expected outputs, sampled weights, identity behavior, or a looser tolerance.
executable_actions.rationale: Audit existing evidence before rerunning anything and reuse an item only when its complete hash identity is exact. Otherwise regenerate only the missing evidence under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2 using the real target model on the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus. The catalog must cover the complete checkpoint, while DUT-consumption coverage is limited to required Transformer-block tensors. Current-run comparison values take precedence; initially absent tolerances may use the authorized framework loose defaults only before the first comparison and must then be frozen.

executable_actions.on_failure: Emit current_contract_valid=false and a precise operator-leaf recertification or capability-repair requirement. A stale or incomplete certificate alone must not trigger RTL repair. If a newly executed real leaf gate fails, route its tool output to contract-guided localization at that leaf and block single-layer promotion.
executable_actions.rationale: Validate the existing certificate first. Execute only the leaf gates identified as missing or stale by the reuse inventory, under the frozen identity. A reusable certificate requires complete per-leaf real-tool evidence, independent target-model boundary values, immutable comparison policy, complete required weight-consumption proof, current boundary contracts, exact artifact hashes, and no pending required gate for this scope.

executable_actions.on_failure: If the operator certificate is not current-valid, mark this action dependency-blocked rather than failed. For stale single-layer evidence, keep reuse disabled and request only missing-gate recertification. For a real single-layer tool failure, retain repair ownership at the connected layer unless a concrete leaf-boundary contradiction is reproduced by targeted leaf replay.
executable_actions.rationale: Single-layer reuse requires a current-valid operator-leaf dependency plus exact-hash scaffold, connected-kernel, functional, golden, real-weight, and semantic-aggregate evidence under the same immutable contract. Revalidation or recertification is not permission to alter the DUT and is distinct from failure-triggered repair.

consumes: exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and simulation source hash manifest
current DDR image and runtime-address manifests
executable_actions.on_failure: If lower certificates are not current-valid, emit dependency-blocked. If exact wrapper or target evidence is ambiguous, block and request bounded approval instead of guessing. For a real functional failure, do not proceed to Vivado; route the failed simulator or classifier evidence to boundary localization. Do not reopen the single layer unless its boundary is contradicted and targeted replay reproduces the failure.
executable_actions.rationale: Create the absent third-layer certificate only from real board-wrapped functional evidence using the exact sources discovered from the current user sample project, the immutable stimulus and target-model Transformer-block golden, complete bound-weight consumption, and AXI/DDR liveness, order, address, and round-trip evidence. This certificate authorizes backend eligibility only and is not a final board-runtime pass.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep repair ownership at the failed higher layer, mark localization or replay inconclusive, and prohibit a lower-layer backtrack or repair. Obtain a valid trace under the same immutable identity and rerun this action; do not infer causality from a final output mismatch alone.
executable_actions.rationale: Localize the earliest violated boundary using cycle, boundary, transaction, tile, logical-index, expected-value, observed-value, contract, and status evidence. A higher-layer failure may target the immediately lower layer only when the trace contains a concrete contradiction and targeted replay with the same checkpoint, stimulus, reference, numeric policy, tolerance, testbench contract, and relevant source hashes reproduces it. Board-to-leaf skipping is forbidden: board failures must first replay/localize the single-layer boundary.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not create an open backtrack request, contamination barrier, or lower-layer repair action. Retain the failure at its current owner and preserve all unrelated current-valid certificates.
produces: SACG scoped backtrack request for one named adjacent lower layer when justified
SACG downstream-consumption trust barrier for the affected certificate and transitive dependents
executable_actions.rationale: Create a SACG blocker only after both contradiction and replay checks pass. The request must name the failed higher gate, violated constraint, contradicted boundary, earliest candidate module, immutable identity, replay command, failed checker to rerun, affected certificate set, and bounded repair owner. No current blocker is assumed from historical records.

consumes: current trusted template bindings and generated implementation
scoped SACG backtrack and trust-barrier records when lower-layer repair was authorized
executable_actions.on_failure: Preserve the failed attempt and its tool output, keep the scoped trust barrier active, and return to contract-guided localization at the same scope. Do not broaden the module set, alter golden outputs or tolerance, or reopen unrelated layers. Escalate to approval only if the causal repair cannot be expressed within the frozen contract and trusted template boundary.
produces: SACG barrier-closure evidence only after fresh promotion
executable_actions.rationale: Repair only the DUT module, loader/harness, instrumentation, or integration proven to violate the contract. Rerun the exact failed checker and owning-scope semantic aggregate before promotion. A leaf change invalidates that leaf aggregate and transitive single/board dependents; a single-layer-only change invalidates single and board dependents; a board-only change invalidates the board certificate. Unaffected sibling evidence remains reusable only when all dependency hashes stay exact.

executable_actions.on_failure: Deny the proposed change, preserve the active contract and evidence, and keep promotion blocked. Never authorize tolerance loosening, golden modification, random expected output, sampled-weight acceptance, or substitution of the exact sample-project wrapper within the current loop.
produces: explicit rejection record when not approved
executable_actions.rationale: Architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy, major-template, or wrapper-identity changes exceed localized repair authority. Even when approved, they must create a new contract and invalidate affected certificates rather than contaminate the current repair loop.

observations: The current Stage 6 verification artifact contract is statically ready: its three repair layers, bottom-up promotion order, semantic evidence gates, boundary-trace schema, and no-unconditional-reopen policy are declared. Pending deadlock-watchdog execution, implementation-package evidence, and board runtime are downstream obligations under the supplied stage-gate policy, not current Stage 6 blockers.

The supplied current-certificate summary is authoritative for reuse: artifact.stage7.operator_leaf_promotion_certificate and artifact.stage7.single_layer_promotion_certificate are present but both have current_contract_valid=false and reuse_allowed=false under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2. Their prior validated trust status and historical pass outcomes do not make them reusable. The board AXI/DDR certificate is absent and also non-reusable.

A stale or invalid current-contract certificate is an evidence-validation condition, not proof of hardware failure. Existing evidence must be audited first; recertification may execute only missing or stale gates under the frozen contract and must not mutate RTL unless a real-tool failure is subsequently localized.

The unified reuse predicate is conjunctive: exact evidence-contract version; exact artifact and dependency hashes; complete checkpoint tensor catalog; deterministic or real stimulus provenance; independent real target-model outputs for the same checkpoint and input; resolved and frozen numeric policy and tolerance; semantic-testbench identity; bound loader/harness identity; executed proof that every required Transformer-block weight was consumed; passed required real-tool gates; current boundary contracts; and no active scoped trust barrier. Artifact presence or a manifest alone is insufficient.

Certificate dependencies are ordered. Operator-leaf current validity is required before single-layer validation; single-layer current validity is required before board AXI/DDR validation. A board certificate additionally requires the exact user-supplied sample-project wrapper and simulation-source hashes plus board-wrapped AXI/DDR functional evidence. It does not substitute for later Vivado, bitstream, or board-runtime evidence.

Failure routing is ownership-preserving by default: a leaf failure stays at the leaf; a single-layer failure stays at connected-layer integration unless a leaf boundary contradiction is reproduced by targeted leaf replay; a board failure stays at the board/AXI/DDR boundary unless a single-layer boundary contradiction is reproduced by targeted single-layer replay. Direct board-to-leaf repair is forbidden, and backend failures do not reopen functional layers without equivalent boundary evidence.

A lower-layer repair authorization requires both a concrete boundary-trace contradiction and a passing same-identity targeted replay, followed by failure_localization_check, causal_repair_context_check, and repair_boundary_check. A final-output mismatch, timeout summary, stale certificate, or historical failure record alone cannot trigger backtrack.

Repair contamination is transitive but bounded. A repaired node invalidates its own certificate and dependent higher-layer certificates, while unrelated sibling evidence remains reusable only when its identity and dependency hashes remain exact. Any change to frozen global semantic inputs starts a new contract rather than a repair-time certificate refresh.

The complete checkpoint catalog may include tensors outside the accelerator, but DUT weight-consumption and golden boundaries cover Transformer blocks only. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain excluded from DUT implementation and acceptance coverage.

The authoritative state_summary.sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. Therefore there is no current SACG-memory blocker to invent or clear; a future scoped backtrack request may be created only from passing contradiction and replay evidence.

The role slice explicitly reports attention semantics, all nine parameter bindings and stage agents, debug schemas, evidence paths, and gate nodes as present. Omitted detailed rows are not treated as missing artifacts.
proposed_actions: Materialize the four Stage 6 policy artifacts and submit them to the canonical gate-DAG auditor without changing the already accepted numeric, pipeline, memory, or board contracts.

Audit and, only where necessary, regenerate semantic evidence under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2 using the immutable checkpoint, stimulus, independent target-model reference, and complete required weight bindings.

Validate or minimally recertify the operator-leaf certificate first, then validate or minimally recertify the single-layer certificate. Keep both reuse-disabled until their current validators explicitly return current_contract_valid=true.

Execute the board AXI/DDR closure only after both lower certificates are current-valid, using exact sample-project source hashes. Issue a board certificate only from complete third-layer semantic evidence; do not infer final hardware pass.
For any failed higher-layer gate, run boundary localization and targeted replay before deciding repair ownership. Keep repair at the failed layer when contradiction or replay evidence is absent.
Create a scoped SACG backtrack request and dependency trust barrier only after replay confirms the immediately lower-layer contradiction; preserve unrelated certificates and evidence.

Apply a trusted-template-bounded repair, rerun the exact failed checker and owning semantic aggregate, and close the scoped barrier only after fresh current-contract promotion. Escalate contract-changing proposals for approval rather than broadening repair.
risks: Promoting either present lower-layer certificate based on artifact presence, historical pass status, or trust_status alone would contaminate the board closure with evidence that is stale or incomplete for real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2.
Treating current-contract validation failure as an RTL failure could cause unconditional reopening and broad churn despite no contradictory boundary trace.

A higher-layer output mismatch can be misattributed to a lower module when the actual cause is connected-layer ordering, AXI backpressure, DDR addressing, runtime ABI, loader binding, or wrapper integration. Earliest-boundary localization is required.

Cross-run mixing of checkpoint, shape, stimulus, reference outputs, precision/cast policy, tolerance, logical/lane order, transfer counts, address map, runtime configuration, implementation hashes, or board-wrapper sources can produce apparently coherent but invalid certificates.

A complete-looking weight manifest can still conceal sampled tensors, excluded required Transformer-block tensors, or a loader that did not execute. Complete-scope hashes and executed consumption evidence are mandatory.

Missing or defective reference, comparator, semantic-harness, or trace capability could be mislabeled as hardware incorrectness. Such cases must remain checker/golden-reference repairs until real RTL evidence exists.

Changing expected outputs, deriving them from RTL, loosening tolerance after observing DUT output, or replacing target-model inference with defaults would invalidate the repair loop rather than fix it.
Using a simplified AXI/DDR wrapper or guessed app-shell target would invalidate the third-layer certificate even if simulation passed.

Over-invalidating all leaf evidence after a localized change would violate bounded reuse, while under-invalidating transitive dependents would permit stale promotion. Invalidation must follow artifact-hash and dependency edges.
The current board certificate is absent and all real board/Vivado/runtime gates remain unexecuted in this Stage 6 evidence; no board or final hardware pass may be claimed.

edges: single-layer current_contract_valid=true -> board AXI/DDR current-contract validation
failed gate tool output -> CCTG/boundary-contract localization
higher-layer boundary contradiction -> same-identity targeted replay
targeted replay pass -> scoped adjacent-layer backtrack authorization
scoped repair -> targeted failed-checker rerun -> owning-scope semantic aggregate -> fresh certificate validation
localized source change -> affected certificate invalidation -> transitive dependent invalidation
missing or stale certificate evidence -> recertification/capability route, not hardware repair
board wrapper source identity -> board certificate validation -> backend eligibility only

output.summary: The unified policy is ready for auditor handoff, but this is not a hardware-pass claim. Both present lower-layer certificates remain non-reusable because their current-contract validators are false under spatialaccagent.real_weight_semantic_evidence.v2; the board certificate is absent. Existing passes must be audited or minimally recertified under the immutable semantic identity, and no higher-layer failure may trigger lower-layer repair without a concrete boundary contradiction, same-identity targeted replay, causal localization, and a scoped repair-boundary decision.
